note: Fourteenth Amendment: equal protection to 'any person within its jurisdiction'. The text does not name aliens; the Supreme Court treats state alienage classifications as suspect (Graham v. Richardson, 1971) and extended equal protection to undocumented children (Plyler v. Doe, 1982).
source: U.S. Const. amend. XIV, s. 1; Yick Wo v. Hopkins, 118 U.S. 356 (1886); Plyler v. Doe, 457 U.S. 202 (1982)

note: Title VII covers national origin but not citizenship (Espinoza v. Farah, 1973). The Immigration Reform and Control Act added citizenship-status discrimination in hiring, limited to citizens, permanent residents, refugees and asylees.
source: 42 U.S.C. 2000e-2; 8 U.S.C. 1324b; Espinoza v. Farah Mfg. Co., 414 U.S. 86 (1973)

note: No prohibition of group-directed hate speech; the First Amendment protects it short of incitement to imminent lawless action or true threats. Federal hate crime law covers violent conduct, not speech.
source: Brandenburg v. Ohio, 395 U.S. 444 (1969); R.A.V. v. City of St. Paul, 505 U.S. 377 (1992); 18 U.S.C. 249

note: No federal statute guarantees equal treatment of migrants as such.
source: Immigration and Nationality Act, 8 U.S.C. ch. 12

note: Charter s. 15 protects 'every individual'. Citizenship is not listed but the Supreme Court recognized it as an analogous ground (Andrews, 1989).
source: Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms, s. 15; Andrews v. Law Society of British Columbia, [1989] 1 SCR 143

note: Federal Canadian Human Rights Act covers race, national or ethnic origin and colour, not citizenship. Several provincial codes (e.g. Ontario) list citizenship.
source: Canadian Human Rights Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. H-6, s. 3; Ontario Human Rights Code, R.S.O. 1990, c. H.19

note: Wilful promotion of hatred against an identifiable group, defined by colour, race, religion, national or ethnic origin and other grounds; nationality and citizenship are not listed.
source: Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, ss. 318(4), 319; R. v. Keegstra, [1990] 3 SCR 697

note: The Immigration and Refugee Protection Act contains no equal-treatment guarantee for migrants; the Multiculturalism Act addresses cultural heritage, not non-citizens.
source: Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, S.C. 2001, c. 27; Canadian Multiculturalism Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. 24 (4th Supp.)

note: Uncodified constitution. The Human Rights Act gives effect to ECHR Article 14, which protects 'everyone' and covers nationality as 'other status' (Gaygusuz v. Austria, 1996).
source: Human Rights Act 1998, Sch. 1, Art. 14; Gaygusuz v. Austria (ECtHR, 1996)

note: 'Race' includes colour, nationality and ethnic or national origins. Nationality was added in 1976 after Ealing LBC v. Race Relations Board (1972) held that 'national origins' excluded it.

note: Stirring up racial hatred; a 'racial group' is defined by colour, race, nationality (including citizenship) or ethnic or national origins.

note: No statute guarantees equal treatment of migrants as such.
source: Immigration Act 1971; Equality Act 2010, Sch. 3 Part 4 (immigration exception)

note: Article 40.1: 'All citizens shall, as human persons, be held equal before the law.' Courts have extended some personal rights to non-citizens by interpretation.

source: Employment Equality Acts 1998-2015, s. 6(2)(h); Equal Status Acts 2000-2018, s. 3(2)(h)

note: Incitement to hatred against a group defined by race, colour, nationality, religion, ethnic or national origins, membership of the Travelling community or sexual orientation.
source: Prohibition of Incitement to Hatred Act 1989, s. 1

note: The International Protection Act and the Immigration Acts contain no general equality guarantee for migrants.

note: Discrimination on the ground of actual or supposed membership or non-membership of an ethnic group, a nation, a so-called race or a religion; 'nation' is read to cover nationality.
Provocation to discrimination, hatred or violence on grounds of origin or membership or non-membership of an ethnic group, a nation, a race or a religion (Loi Pleven, 1972).
source: Loi du 29 juillet 1881 sur la liberte de la presse, art. 24

note: The Code on the entry and residence of foreigners (CESEDA) contains no general equality guarantee.
Article 3(1): 'All persons are equal before the law'; Article 3(3) lists origin, race, language and homeland. Some rights (assembly, association, free movement, occupation) are reserved to Germans.
The General Equal Treatment Act covers race and ethnic origin but not nationality, following EU Directive 2000/43.
Incitement to hatred against a national, racial, religious or ethnic group or sections of the population; foreigners living in Germany are recognized as a section of the population.
The Residence Act contains no general equality guarantee for foreigners.
Article 1 applies to 'all persons in the Netherlands', a territorial rather than citizenship scope, without naming foreigners.
Equal treatment act lists nationality among the protected grounds.

Group insult and incitement on grounds of race, religion or belief, sexual orientation or disability. Nationality is not listed; 'race' is read to include national or ethnic origin (as in the Wilders case on Moroccans).
source: Wetboek van Strafrecht, arts. 137c, 137d; Hoge Raad, 6 July 2021

note: The Aliens Act contains no general equality guarantee.
Article 10 guarantees equality to Belgians, but Article 191 expressly extends to every foreigner on Belgian territory the protection granted to persons and property, save exceptions by law.
The Anti-Racism Law protects nationality, so-called race, colour, descent and national or ethnic origin.
source: Loi du 30 juillet 1981 tendant a reprimer certains actes inspires par le racisme ou la xenophobie, art. 4

note: Incitement to discrimination, hatred or violence on the same grounds, including nationality.
The Aliens Act of 1980 contains no general equality guarantee.
source: Loi du 15 decembre 1980 sur l'acces au territoire

note: Article 7 guarantees equality to citizens. The constitutional act on racial discrimination (1973) bars distinctions on race, colour, descent or national or ethnic origin, from which the Constitutional Court derives equal treatment of foreigners among themselves.
source: B-VG, Art. 7; BVG zur Durchfuhrung des Internationalen Ubereinkommens uber die Beseitigung aller Formen rassischer Diskriminierung, BGBl. 390/1973

note: The Equal Treatment Act covers ethnic affiliation but not nationality.

Incitement against a group defined by race, colour, language, religion or belief, nationality, descent or national or ethnic origin, sex, disability, age or sexual orientation (nationality added in the 2015 reform).

Article 8(1): 'Every person is equal before the law'; Article 8(2) bars discrimination on origin, race and other grounds.
No general anti-discrimination statute; only sectoral acts on gender and disability.
Discrimination and incitement on grounds of race, ethnicity, religion or sexual orientation; the Federal Supreme Court holds that foreigners or asylum seekers as such are not a protected group.
The Foreign Nationals and Integration Act directs authorities to promote integration and protection against discrimination, without an individual remedy.
Instrument of Government affirms the equal worth of all and bars discrimination on ethnic origin; it allows special limits on foreigners' rights by law.
'Ethnicity' covers national or ethnic origin, skin colour or similar circumstance; nationality is not listed.
Agitation against a group with reference to race, colour, national or ethnic origin, religion, sexual orientation or transgender identity.
The Aliens Act contains no general equality guarantee.
No general equality clause. Section 70 bars deprivation of civil and political rights for creed or descent only.
Prohibitions on discrimination for race, colour, national or ethnic origin and belief; nationality is not listed.
source: Lov om forbud mod forskelsbehandling pa grund af race m.v.; Lov om forbud mod forskelsbehandling pa arbejdsmarkedet

note: Public threats, insults or degradation of a group for race, colour, national or ethnic origin, belief, sexual orientation or gender identity.
The Aliens Act contains no general equality guarantee.

Article 3 is framed for citizens, but Article 10(2) requires the legal condition of foreigners to conform to international norms and treaties, and the Constitutional Court applies equality to foreigners for inviolable rights (Judgment 120/1967).
Implementation of EU Directive 2000/43 covers race and ethnic origin.
Propaganda and incitement on racial, ethnic, national or religious grounds.
source: Codice penale, art. 604-bis (formerly Legge 654/1975 as amended by Legge 205/1993)

note: The Consolidated Immigration Act defines discriminatory acts, including those against a foreigner solely because of that status, with a dedicated civil action.
Article 13(1): foreigners enjoy the public freedoms of Title I on the terms set by treaties and law; Article 14 guarantees equality to Spaniards.
Criminal prohibitions of discrimination in employment and public services for belonging to an ethnic group, race or nation; Law 15/2022 adds a general equal treatment regime.
Incitement to hatred for racist reasons or for belonging to an ethnic group, race or nation, or national origin, among other grounds.
The Foreigners Act guarantees foreigners rights in conditions of equality with Spaniards and defines discriminatory acts against foreigners.
Article 15(1): foreigners and stateless persons in Portugal enjoy the same rights and duties as Portuguese citizens, with listed exceptions.
Prohibition of discrimination on racial and ethnic origin, colour, nationality, ancestry and territory of origin.
Incitement to hatred or violence for race, colour, ethnic or national origin, ancestry, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or disability.
The Foreigners Act sets entry and residence rules; equal treatment rests on Article 15 of the Constitution.
Article 4 guarantees equality to Greeks, but Article 5(2) guarantees all persons on Greek territory full protection of life, honour and liberty irrespective of nationality, race or language.
Equal treatment law covers race, colour, national or ethnic origin and descent; nationality is excluded, following the EU directives.
Public incitement to violence or hatred for race, colour, religion, descent, national or ethnic origin, sexual orientation, gender identity or disability.
source: Law 927/1979, art. 1, as amended by Law 4285/2014

note: The Migration Code governs entry, residence and integration without a general equality guarantee.
No general equality guarantee. Section 117 bars discrimination against residents of other states only.
source: Commonwealth Constitution, s. 117; Street v. Queensland Bar Association (1989)

note: Race, colour, descent or national or ethnic origin; nationality is not covered (Macabenta, 1998). Nationality complaints under ILO Convention 111 go to conciliation only.

note: Civil prohibition of acts likely to offend, insult, humiliate or intimidate because of race, colour or national or ethnic origin; some states add criminal offences.
The Migration Act contains no equality guarantee.

Bill of Rights Act s. 19 protects everyone from discrimination on the grounds in the Human Rights Act, which defines ethnic or national origins to include nationality or citizenship. The Bill of Rights is an ordinary statute.
source: New Zealand Bill of Rights Act 1990, s. 19; Human Rights Act 1993, s. 21(1)(g)

note: Prohibited grounds include ethnic or national origins, which includes nationality or citizenship.
Inciting racial disharmony against a group by reference to colour, race or ethnic or national origins, read with the s. 21 definition that includes nationality or citizenship.
The Immigration Act contains no equality guarantee.
Article 14: 'All of the people (kokumin) are equal under the law.' The Supreme Court extends constitutional rights to foreigners except those that by nature apply only to nationals (McLean, 1978).

note: No general anti-discrimination statute, but the Labor Standards Act bars discrimination in working conditions on nationality, creed or social status.
source: Labor Standards Act (Act No. 49 of 1947), art. 3

note: The Hate Speech Elimination Act names 'persons originating from outside Japan' but contains no prohibition or sanction; Kawasaki City added criminal penalties in 2019.
source: Act on the Promotion of Efforts to Eliminate Unfair Discriminatory Speech and Behavior against Persons Originating from Outside Japan (Act No. 68 of 2016); Kawasaki City Ordinance (2019)

note: The Immigration Control and Refugee Recognition Act contains no equality guarantee.
source: Immigration Control and Refugee Recognition Act (Cabinet Order No. 319 of 1951)

note: Article 11: 'All citizens shall be equal before the law.' The Constitutional Court recognizes foreigners as holders of basic rights that belong to human beings (99Hun-Ma494, 2001).
No general anti-discrimination statute, but the Labor Standards Act bars discrimination on gender, nationality, religion or social status.
No hate speech law; bills for a comprehensive anti-discrimination act have not passed.

source: Act on the Employment, etc. of Foreign Workers, art. 22; Framework Act on Treatment of Foreigners Residing in the Republic of Korea, art. 10

note: Article 7: 'All citizens of the Republic of China' are equal. Constitutional interpretations extend personal liberty protections to foreigners (J.Y. Interpretations 708 and 710).
source: Constitution of the Republic of China, Art. 7; J.Y. Interpretation No. 708 (2013)

note: The Employment Service Act bars discrimination on race, class, language, religion, place of origin and other grounds; nationality is not listed.
No general hate speech law.

Article 14 guarantees equality before the law to 'any person', but Article 15's ban on discrimination protects citizens only.
No general anti-discrimination statute.
Promoting enmity between groups on grounds of religion, race, place of birth, residence, language, caste or community; nationality is not listed.
source: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, s. 196 (formerly Indian Penal Code, s. 153A)

note: Foreigners law (Immigration and Foreigners Act 2025) contains no equality guarantee.
Articles 28D(1) and 28I(2) protect 'every person' (setiap orang), including against discriminatory treatment, without naming foreigners.
The law on racial and ethnic discrimination covers race and ethnicity; the Manpower Act bars discrimination without listing grounds.
source: UU No. 40 Tahun 2008; UU No. 13 Tahun 2003, art. 5

note: The 2024 amendment of the Electronic Information Law penalizes incitement to hatred based on race, nationality (kebangsaan), ethnicity, colour, religion, belief, sex or disability; earlier text referred to ethnic, religious, racial and inter-group (SARA) hatred.
source: UU No. 1 Tahun 2024, art. 28(2); UU No. 40 Tahun 2008, art. 16

note: The Immigration Act contains no equality guarantee.

No general anti-discrimination statute.

note: The Immigration Act contains no equality guarantee.

No general anti-discrimination statute; a comprehensive bill has been pending for years.

source: Immigration Act 13 of 2002, s. 2; National Action Plan to Combat Racism, Racial Discrimination, Xenophobia and Related Intolerance (2019)

note: Article 17 protects 'all persons' and bars discrimination on gender, race, colour, ethnic origin, religion and status.
The Labour Act bars discrimination on gender, race, colour, ethnic origin, religion, creed and status; nationality is not listed.
No hate speech law.

Article 27 protects 'every person'; grounds include ethnic or social origin, colour, culture and birth.
The Employment Act bars discrimination on nationality, among other grounds.
Hate speech offence protects ethnic groups, defined by colour, race, religion or ethnic or national origins.
source: National Cohesion and Integration Act 2008, ss. 2, 13, 62

note: The Citizenship and Immigration Act contains no equality guarantee.
Article 5 guarantees equality to 'Brazilians and foreigners residing in the country'.
Crimes of discrimination for race, colour, ethnicity, religion or national origin (procedencia nacional).
Inciting discrimination or prejudice on the same grounds.
The Migration Law guarantees migrants equality with nationals and makes repudiation of xenophobia and discrimination a principle; it replaced the 1980 Foreigners Statute.
Article 20: foreigners enjoy all the civil rights of citizens.
Discriminatory acts on grounds such as race, religion, nationality, ideology, sex and social condition.
Propaganda or incitement to persecution or hatred for race, religion, nationality or political ideas.
The Migration Law recognizes migration as a human right and defines discriminatory acts against migrants.
Article 19 secures rights to 'all persons'.
Anti-discrimination law lists race or ethnicity, nationality and socioeconomic status among the grounds.
Fines for publications or broadcasts intended to promote hatred or hostility for race, sex, religion or nationality; media only.
The Migration Law guarantees equality and non-discrimination for foreigners; it replaced Decree-Law 1094 of 1975.
Article 1 guarantees human rights to all persons; Article 33 states that foreigners enjoy the human rights and guarantees of the Constitution.
Federal anti-discrimination law lists ethnic or national origin and migratory status among the grounds.

The Migration Law guarantees migrants equal treatment without discrimination regardless of migratory status.
Article 100: foreigners enjoy the same civil rights as Colombians, subject to limits by law.
Criminal offence of discrimination for race, nationality, sex, sexual orientation, disability and other grounds.
Harassment and promotion of hostility on the same grounds, including nationality.
The Comprehensive Migration Policy law sets equality and non-discrimination as principles without an individual remedy.
